representation: MODRISS JSON DSL mapped to SPEM 2.0

roleDefinitions.name: Release Engineer
responsibilities: Owns release plan, versioning, approvals, and deployment evidence

roleDefinitions.name: Cloud Platform Engineer
responsibilities: Hardens infrastructure, IAM, environment configuration, and deployment automation

roleDefinitions.name: Application Engineer
responsibilities: Reviews generated code, completes application configuration, and fixes implementation gaps

roleDefinitions.name: Security Engineer
responsibilities: Reviews secrets, access control, dependencies, and security controls

roleDefinitions.name: Quality Engineer
responsibilities: Defines test evidence and verifies functional and non-functional acceptance

roleDefinitions.name: Service Owner
responsibilities: Accepts operational readiness, rollback posture, and production handover

taskDefinitions.name: Review project structure and generated templates
taskDefinitions.purpose: Review project structure and generated templates
steps: Inspect template, source, configuration, documentation, and pipeline files in the artifact explorer.
Identify entry points, Lambda handlers, infrastructure resources, parameters, outputs, and generated deployment instructions.
Compare the generated structure with the PSM deployable slice and record missing or unexpected components.
exitCriteria: Project inventory and PSM-to-file trace are recorded
validationRules: Every deployable resource has an identifiable template or source owner

taskDefinitions.name: Establish source-control and release baseline
steps: Create a dedicated branch or repository according to team policy.
Commit the unmodified generated baseline with generator, PSM revision, and generation timestamp recorded.
Tag or otherwise identify the baseline so later refinements are reviewable.
exitCriteria: Baseline is versioned and reproducible

taskDefinitions.name: Route structural gaps back to the PSM
taskDefinitions.purpose: Route structural gaps back to the PSM
steps: Classify each gap as a PSM modeling defect, generator limitation, or legitimate implementation refinement.
For missing resources, permissions, integrations, or policies, update and validate the PSM before regenerating artifacts.
Record the reason for any approved hand-maintained template extension.
exitCriteria: PSM feedback and local refinements have named owners
validationRules: Architecture decisions are not hidden only in generated files

taskDefinitions.name: Complete repository hygiene
steps: Add repository documentation, ownership, license, ignore rules, and contribution instructions required by the organization.
Confirm generated documentation names the service, supported environments, and deployment prerequisites.
Ensure build outputs and local credentials are excluded from source control.
exitCriteria: Repository can be safely shared and reviewed
validationRules: Repository contains no generated build output or credential material

taskDefinitions.name: Define parameter and environment contract
steps: List required parameters, outputs, domains, regions, account IDs, tags, feature flags, and external endpoints.
Provide validated values or references for development, test, staging, and production.
Document defaults, allowed ranges, and the owner for every environment-specific value.
entryCriteria: Deployment templates and runtime configuration are known
exitCriteria: All environment values have a documented source and owner
validationRules: Production values are not copied into non-production configuration

taskDefinitions.name: Configure secret references and encryption
steps: Replace inline credentials, tokens, and sensitive defaults with approved secret-manager or parameter-store references.
Verify encryption keys, rotation expectations, and access paths for each secret or protected data store.
Document bootstrap steps that create secrets before deployment.
exitCriteria: Secrets are externalized and bootstrap steps are reproducible
validationRules: No secret value is committed to source control or template defaults

taskDefinitions.name: Review IAM and deployment permissions
steps: Review execution roles, resource policies, and CI/CD identities against least-privilege requirements.
Separate deployment permissions from application runtime permissions.
Record exceptions, approval owners, and expiration dates for elevated access.
entryCriteria: Infrastructure and delivery identities are defined
exitCriteria: Required permissions are approved and bounded
validationRules: No wildcard permission remains without documented justification

taskDefinitions.name: Implement repeatable build and deployment pipeline
taskDefinitions.purpose: Implement repeatable build and deployment pipeline
steps: Configure the approved CI/CD workflow to restore dependencies, build, package, validate, and deploy the artifact.
Pin or record runtime, build-image, and dependency-resolution versions.
Require review and controlled promotion between environments.
entryCriteria: Environment contract and deployment identities are available
exitCriteria: A pipeline can produce a uniquely identifiable release candidate
validationRules: Build and deploy steps do not depend on a developer workstation

taskDefinitions.name: Run reproducible build and infrastructure validation
taskDefinitions.purpose: Run reproducible build and infrastructure validation
steps: Build and package the project using the delivery pipeline.
Run the project's infrastructure/template validation and capture the results.
Verify generated deployment artifacts match the tagged source revision.
exitCriteria: Build and template validation evidence is retained
validationRules: Build succeeds from a clean environment

taskDefinitions.name: Assess dependencies and security findings
steps: Run approved dependency, secret, and infrastructure security scans.
Triage findings by severity and exploitability; fix blockers or obtain time-bound risk acceptance.
Verify logging, encryption, retention, and data-handling controls meet the PSM intent.
exitCriteria: Security findings are resolved or formally accepted
validationRules: No unresolved critical finding proceeds without explicit risk acceptance

taskDefinitions.name: Deploy to staging and execute acceptance tests
taskDefinitions.purpose: Deploy to staging and execute acceptance tests
steps: Deploy the exact candidate through the pipeline to a controlled non-production environment.
Execute smoke, integration, contract, and business acceptance tests for the deployable slice.
Record test data constraints, results, defects, and any accepted deviations.
exitCriteria: Acceptance evidence covers critical user and integration paths
validationRules: Tests target the deployed candidate as well as local code

taskDefinitions.name: Verify observability and operational signals
steps: Confirm logs, metrics, traces, dashboards, and alarms are emitted for critical paths.
Trigger representative failure and recovery scenarios to verify alert routing and diagnostic context.
Set practical thresholds and identify the team that responds to each alert.
exitCriteria: Critical operational signals and alert ownership are verified
validationRules: An operator can detect and diagnose a failed critical path

taskDefinitions.name: Create release, rollback, and communication plan
taskDefinitions.purpose: Create release, rollback, and communication plan
steps: Define release scope, version, deployment sequence, approvals, maintenance window, and stakeholder communications.
Document rollback triggers, steps, data considerations, decision owner, and expected recovery time.
Rehearse rollback or recovery in non-production when the change affects data, interfaces, or critical availability.
exitCriteria: Release and rollback plan are approved by accountable owners
validationRules: Rollback does not rely on undocumented manual knowledge

taskDefinitions.name: Obtain production readiness approval
steps: Review release scope, risk, verification evidence, security findings, operational readiness, and rollback posture.
Capture go/no-go decision, approvers, constraints, and follow-up actions.
Confirm support and business stakeholders understand the release window and success criteria.
entryCriteria: Release plan and evidence are available
exitCriteria: Go/no-go decision is recorded
validationRules: Production deployment has an accountable approver

taskDefinitions.name: Complete operations handover
steps: Publish runbooks for deployment, rollback, common incidents, access requests, and escalation.
Assign service ownership, on-call coverage, dashboards, alerts, service objectives, and support contacts.
Transfer repository, pipeline, and environment access according to the operating model.
exitCriteria: Operations team can support the deployed service
validationRules: Runbooks identify owners and escalation paths

taskDefinitions.name: Execute production validation and close release
taskDefinitions.purpose: Execute production validation and close release
steps: Deploy the approved release candidate using the documented pipeline and plan.
Perform post-deployment smoke checks, monitor health signals, and confirm business and technical success criteria.
Close the release or invoke rollback; record lessons and feed recurring issues to the PSM or generator backlog.
exitCriteria: Production outcome and follow-up actions are recorded
validationRules: Production health is checked before the release is closed

workProductDefinitions.name: Generated Project Baseline
workProductDefinitions.description: Reviewed, version-controlled output generated from the approved PSM

workProductDefinitions.name: Environment Configuration Contract
workProductDefinitions.description: Per-environment parameters, secrets references, account/region bindings, and ownership

workProductDefinitions.name: Security Review Record
workProductDefinitions.description: Least-privilege, secret handling, dependency, and data-protection evidence

workProductDefinitions.name: Verification Evidence
workProductDefinitions.description: Build, validation, test, and quality-gate results

workProductDefinitions.name: Release & Rollback Plan
workProductDefinitions.description: Version, deployment sequence, approvals, rollback steps, and communications

workProductDefinitions.name: Operations Handover Pack
workProductDefinitions.description: Runbooks, dashboards, alarms, support ownership, and post-release checks

guidance.name: Generated output is a controlled baseline
guidance.text: Treat generated files as a PSM-derived baseline: review every generated change, commit it to source control, and feed structural defects back to the PSM instead of repeatedly patching generated output.

guidance.name: Environment parity with explicit differences
guidance.text: Keep development, test, staging, and production configuration structurally equivalent. Record intentional differences as parameters or approved environment exceptions.

guidance.name: No secrets in artifacts
guidance.text: Store secret values only in the approved secret manager or CI/CD secret store; generated templates and repositories contain references, never secret material.

guidance.name: Evidence before promotion
guidance.text: Promotion requires reproducible build, validation, test, and security evidence for the exact release candidate.

guidance.name: Rehearse recovery
guidance.text: A release is not ready until rollback, data protection, alerting, and ownership are demonstrably usable by the on-call team.

sourceOfTruth: The project work tracker stores one process-run record per release candidate.
The release record stores the exact artifact, configuration, test, and deployment revisions.

aggregation.rule: Aggregate by release candidate, team, release, and product; never average away a blocking finding.
aggregation.teamCoordination: Publish a shared dependency board with owner, dependency type, due date, and escalation path.
aggregation.reviewCadence: Daily delivery coordination, candidate review, and post-release service review.

metrics.name: Eligible task completion
metrics.cadence: each workday and at gate review
metrics.interpretation: Visibility only; never substitute for a usable release candidate.

metrics.name: Release evidence completeness
metrics.formula: required release evidence items present for the exact candidate / required evidence items
metrics.interpretation: No promotion with missing evidence; exceptions are explicit and time-bound.

metrics.name: Open blocking findings
metrics.interpretation: Must be zero or covered by an explicit, time-bound risk acceptance.

metrics.name: Escaped-defect rate
metrics.formula: defects first detected after release acceptance, categorized by source stage
metrics.interpretation: Feed recurring causes back to the earliest correct source of change.

governance.gate: A release candidate is promotable only when the exact artifact, configuration, evidence, approval, and rollback identity are recorded.

processEngine.description: Refines generated AWS SAM project artifacts into a reviewed, verified, releasable, and operable deployment package.

deliverable.name: Approved deployment package
deliverable.description: A versioned artifact set with configuration, verification evidence, release approval, rollback plan, and operations handover.

loop.guidance: When verification, approval, or operational rehearsal exposes a defect, correct the source PSM or artifact baseline, regenerate where necessary, and repeat the affected readiness stages.

processEngine.spemMapping: MODRISS extension realized as an Activity(kind = Iteration) containing process Activities and WorkSequences.

phases.name: Inspect & Baseline Generated Project
phases.objective: Turn the PSM-generated project into a traceable, reviewed, version-controlled release baseline and identify model changes that must return to PSM.
entryCriteria: Artifacts were generated from an approved PSM
A target repository and release owner are available
exitCriteria: Generated files are inventoried and committed
Implementation gaps are classified as artifact refinements or PSM feedback

stages.name: Inventory Generated Output
stages.objective: Understand exactly what was generated and how it maps to the intended deployment.

stages.name: Classify Refinements
stages.objective: Keep architecture changes in the model and implementation-specific refinements in the project.

phases.name: Harden Environment & Delivery Configuration
phases.objective: Make the generated project safe and repeatable across target environments without embedding secrets or account-specific assumptions.
entryCriteria: Target environments and account ownership are known
exitCriteria: Environment contract, least-privilege access, and CI/CD configuration are reviewed

stages.name: Externalize Environment Configuration
stages.objective: Separate deploy-time configuration and secret references from source and templates.

stages.name: Harden Delivery Automation
stages.objective: Create a controlled path for building and deploying the exact release candidate.

phases.name: Verify Release Candidate
phases.objective: Prove that the exact release candidate is buildable, secure, functional, observable, and deployable before production approval.
entryCriteria: Pipeline and environment contract are available
exitCriteria: Required verification evidence is attached to the release candidate
Defects are resolved or explicitly accepted

stages.name: Build & Static Verification
stages.objective: Check packaging, template validity, dependencies, and security posture.

stages.name: Deploy & Exercise Non-Production
stages.objective: Demonstrate the release candidate in a production-like environment.

phases.name: Approve Release & Operational Handover
phases.objective: Prepare a controlled production release with recovery, ownership, communications, and post-deployment verification defined.
entryCriteria: Production deployment window and approvers are known
exitCriteria: Deployment package is approved, recoverable, and handed to operations

stages.name: Plan Release & Recovery
stages.objective: Make production deployment and failure recovery deliberate and executable.

stages.name: Handover & Post-Deployment Validation
stages.objective: Ensure the service can be supported after deployment and verify production health immediately after release.

workSequences.guidance: When verification, approval, or operational rehearsal exposes a defect, correct the source PSM or artifact baseline, regenerate where necessary, and repeat the affected readiness stages.

workflows.name: PSM feedback and regeneration
workflows.trigger: A generated artifact reveals a missing or incorrect resource, integration, permission, or policy.
steps: Record the artifact gap and affected release candidate.
Correct and validate the PSM source model.
Regenerate artifacts, reapply approved extensions, and repeat affected verification tasks.

workflows.name: Release-candidate rework
workflows.trigger: Verification, approval, or post-deployment validation fails.
steps: Contain the issue and decide whether to fix forward or roll back.
Correct the baseline, configuration, PSM, or generator as appropriate.
Create a new versioned candidate and repeat the required gates.
